name: Siltframe Deep-Pocket Infiltration Rig
description: Built around a long overshirt in silt-green matte ripstop — not a jacket, not quite a coat, landing at mid-thigh — this rig succeeds by looking like it belongs everywhere and nowhere specific. The overshirt has fourteen pockets total, only four of which are externally visible; the rest are internal panel pockets accessed through slotted seams along the side chest, inner hem, and a full-width lower-back channel designed to double as a flat equipment carry. The fabric is woven with an irregular charcoal grid pattern that breaks up body outline on low-resolution surveillance cameras. Underneath, a close-fit base layer in near-black burgundy thermal-weave manages temperature and provides a second surface of scanner-disrupting material. The trousers are slim-cut in dark storm-grey with aug-routing channels along the outer thigh — reinforced conduit seams that guide power cables from leg prosthetics or chrome augmentation without pinching or snagging. A detachable cargo panel can be added or removed from the left thigh via snap-bar. Footwear is a mid-ankle boot in dark green synthetic suede over a rubberized low-profile sole, with magnetic-close side panels instead of laces — fast on, fast off. A narrow hood is stored collapsed inside the overshirt's rear collar and deploys in two seconds, covering the neck and the back of the skull without obscuring peripheral vision.
functionality: Fourteen pockets (ten concealed); surveillance-disrupting irregular weave pattern; scanner-resistant dual-layer construction; aug-routing conduit seams on outer thigh for chrome leg hardware; detachable cargo panel; deployable stored hood; magnetic-close fast-off footwear; flat equipment carry in rear channel
what_it_says: Whoever wears this has thought through every second of the job before leaving the safe house. The pocket count alone signals professional patience. The silt-green reads as maintenance or environmental services to a casual eye — but the precise fit and the lack of any corporate logo says independent. This is a runner who values invisibility over reputation.
worn_by: chrome-leg aug users needing routing accommodation
manufacturer: Ashveil Workshop — independent street fabricator, unlicensed, Shelf-Circuit border
story_hooks: A security sweep uses a new thermal-layer scanner that sees through the outer ripstop — the runner's burgundy base layer is now the only thing between them and detection, and it's showing heat bloom from a concealed power cell.

The collapsed hood deploys during a chase but the magnetic boot panels snap open on a magnetized loading dock floor, leaving one boot behind — the runner has to complete the job and the extraction half-barefoot.
Someone else is wearing the same Ashveil rig at the target site — either a coincidence, a setup, or the fixer double-booked the job.

physical_description.visual_profile: A deliberately unremarkable silhouette — intentionally designed to fade into urban environments. The silt-green overshirt dominates, hanging straight and utilitarian at mid-thigh, paired with fitted storm-grey trousers and dark ankle boots. The overall impression is functional anonymity: practical enough for street work, nondescript enough to avoid algorithmic flagging. Slightly military in bearing without the regimentation.
physical_description.fit: Overshirt is relaxed but not baggy — structured enough to maintain clean lines for surveillance evasion. Base layer is compression-tight beneath. Trousers are slim through hip and thigh, tapering to ankle. Boots grip the calf without restriction. Every element permits rapid movement and equipment access without excess fabric.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte ripstop synthetic in silt-green (overshirt); near-black burgundy thermal-weave base layer; storm-grey performance blend trousers; synthetic suede over rubberized sole boots. All materials are scanner-disrupting composites.
physical_description.texture: Ripstop has a tight, almost invisible grid weave that catches light unevenly. Charcoal pattern breaks up visual continuity. Base layer is smooth, friction-fitted. Trousers have a subtle technical sheen. Boot suede is velveted matte with raised conduit seams along outer thigh.
physical_description.color_scheme: Silt-green overshirt with charcoal grid pattern. Burgundy base layer visible at collar and cuffs. Storm-grey trousers. Dark green boots. Minimal contrast — palette is muted, low-visibility greens and greys with deep burgundy undertones.
physical_description.closures: Overshirt: magnetic snap front placket (silent, no zipper rattle). Trousers: friction-fit waistband with discrete tension adjustment. Boots: magnetic-close side panels for rapid deployment. Hood: friction-lock internal seal.
distinctive_features: Fourteen total pockets — four external, ten hidden in internal panels and slotted seams
Full-width lower-back equipment channel accessed through panel seams
Charcoal grid weave pattern designed to defeat low-res surveillance
Scanner-disrupting material woven throughout overshirt and base layer
Aug-routing channels along outer thigh with reinforced conduit seams
Detachable snap-bar cargo panel on left thigh
Rapid-deploy hood stored collapsed in rear collar — deploys in ~2 seconds
Magnetic closures throughout (silent, aug-compatible, non-conductive alert points)
No visible branding; Ashveil Workshop maker's micro-etch on interior collar only
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3–4 (working class with specialized black-market access). Street-fabricated, unlicensed, purpose-built for infiltration work. Too functional and unmarked to be corpo Tier 1–2, too intentional to be salvage Tier 5.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by runners, infiltrators, black-market couriers, sub-grid operators, and anyone needing to move through the city without catching algorithmic attention. Signals competence, street credentials, and willingness to operate outside licensed channels. Ashveil Workshop reputation adds mystique — independent fabricators are romanticized but legally invisible.
physical_description.condition_typical: Delivered in pristine condition but designed to weather. After 2–3 months of use, the ripstop develops micro-creases that enhance the disruption pattern. Pocket seams may fray slightly. Magnetic snaps collect trace wear but remain functional. Boots develop scuff marks that blend into the aesthetic rather than detracting from it. The rig looks better worn — breaking in is part of the design philosophy.
